{"task": {"id": "I_kwDOUDROfM8AAAABf9ZXEA", "item_id": "PVTI_lAHOAHSLSM4BlR_zzhJaRl8", "project_id": "PVT_kwHOAHSLSM4BlR_z", "number": 392, "title": "Unify TranslateGemma 4B JA→EN / EN→JA into one Translation node with TEXT language ports", "body": "## Goal

Consolidate the two current TranslateGemma 4B graph Node types (`TranslateGemmaJaEn` and `TranslateGemmaEnJa`) into **one multilingual Translation Node**, because they already use the **exact same pinned ONNX checkpoint** `onnx-community/translategemma-text-4b-it-ONNX@f7874a1ac60758872a4f78aac0df95b17b776994`, dtype q4, WebGPU. Only the source/target language values differ.

The UI should have **one Add Node entry: "Translation"**, with **"TranslateGemma 4B" as the secondary model subtitle**, consistent with the approach chosen for PLaMo in #391. This is an ordinary translation Node, not a new model, model-size selector, or a switch in Settings.

## Ports and behavior

- Replace the two direction-specific Node types with **one stable new concrete type** (e.g. `TranslateGemma4B`), rather than keeping duplicate direction-specific Node entries.
- Preserve existing committed and preview translation contracts: inputs `text: TEXT`, `provisional: TEXT`, `id: NUMBER`, `provisionalId: NUMBER`; outputs `source`, `text`, `error`, `id`, and `provisionalSource`, `provisionalText`, `provisionalError`, `provisionalId`. Existing atomic groups, ID matching, preview clearing/replacement, queue ordering, Stop, Cancel, and errors must continue to work.
- Preserve optional `context: TEXT` and its existing 4,000-character reference-only behavior. Ensure context prompt accurately uses the source and target language of the **individual translation request**, not a stale language fixed when the Worker was loaded.
- Add **optional `source_lang: TEXT`** and **optional `target_lang: TEXT`** input ports. Like PLaMo, language codes are supplied via other Text Node outputs, **not Settings controls**, and language-only updates do not trigger translation. Multiple updates and grouped delivery use existing scheduler snapshot semantics.
- Unconnected defaults: **source `ja` and target `en`**, matching the present JA→EN implementation, **unless upstream TranslateGemma's actual model/template defaults are verified to provide better well-defined behavior**. In all cases, document the defaults precisely, send source/target explicitly to the model when required, and **never assume automatic source detection** or an unspecified default that the model does not support. If a default decision changes after investigating upstream, document why.
- Validate explicit language codes against TranslateGemma's **actual supported language set / tokenizer format**; do not artificially restrict to Japanese and English and do not pretend arbitrary language codes work. Test `ja`↔`en` and representative other officially supported pairs using the existing structured language-tag API.
- Each accepted `text` or `provisional` input gets an **immutable snapshot of source_lang, target_lang, context, id**, including grouped delivery. Changes to language/context affect *future* jobs only; no cross-job contamination. Language-only or context-only input never invokes inference.

## Model loading and runtime

- Inspect and update `web/translategemma-worker.js` and `web/translation-nodes.js`: currently the Worker chooses `direction='ja-en'|'en-ja'` during **load**. Load the shared model once per Node session; pass `source_lang_code` / `target_lang_code` as **per-request translation arguments** rather than requiring a new Worker/model load to switch direction.
- The existing standard structured `[{role:'user',content:[{type:'text',source_lang_code,target_lang_code,text}]}]` model call must keep working. Update `web/translategemma-context.js` context-aware prompt generation to accept per-request source/target codes and correctly name the languages; preserve safety checks and token budgets.
- Reuse the exact existing pinned model weights, verified `ModelAssetCache`, manifest, WebGPU inference and offline-cache behavior. **Do not duplicate/re-download weights simply because the graph Node type is consolidated**; do not bundle weights or add remote inference.
- Keep TranslateGemma distinct from PLaMo: they share the general "Translation" visible function label but keep separate model subtitles, code paths, license obligations, and capabilities.

## Graph / UI / docs / tests

- Replace old types in `extension/graph.js`, `extension/graph-runtime.js`, `extension/graph-palette.js`, `extension/graph-model-preparation.js`, graph preferences, help, models/Playground and sample graphs. Only **one** TranslateGemma Add Node item.
- Avoid unnecessary legacy branches or permanent duplicated Node types. **Do not silently change the meaning of existing saved JA→EN or EN→JA graphs**: preserve translation direction during any narrowly scoped migration to the unified Node (e.g. explicit values connected or defined), or report actionable validation/recreation guidance. Preserve user connections and the reference context where possible. No separate permanent compatibility runtime.
- Keep the model library/Models page's **single shared TranslateGemma model card** and license link.
- Test language-only updates, grouped text/id/lang/context events, immutable job snapshots, quick direction switches during queued translations, context prompts for both directions, errors, previews, Stop/Cancel, model cache/preparation and graph save/reload, and existing ASR→TranslateGemma→KeyedTextPair/Display flow.
- Update unit tests and independent TranslateGemma Playground (web/nodes/translategemma/) to exercise the **same single-model, dynamic-language behavior**, including Japanese→English, English→Japanese, and an actually supported third-language pair. Run deterministic default CI without multi-GB model downloads; keep real-model smoke as opt-in.

## Acceptance criteria

- [ ] Exactly one **Translation / TranslateGemma 4B** Node is in Add Node.
- [ ] Optional TEXT `source_lang` and `target_lang` ports select the translation direction; no direction setting or separate JA→EN/EN→JA Node.
- [ ] The same loaded checkpoint processes both directions and supported other languages on the actual browser WebGPU runtime, without reinitialization for direction changes.
- [ ] Optional `context`, original translation outputs, IDs, previews, lifecycle and full model cache behavior still work.
- [ ] Defaults are explicitly defined and verified; no ungrounded claim of auto-detection or multilingual support.
- [ ] Graph persistence and existing directional graph behavior are addressed without parallel legacy runtime nodes or silent reversal of translations.
- [ ] Automated unit, MV3 and Playground tests and active documentation reflect the unified Node.

## References

- Previous related changes: #391 (PLaMo multilingual Translation name/ports), #385 (PLaMo initial implementation)
- Current code: `web/translategemma-worker.js`, `web/translategemma-context.js`, `web/translation-nodes.js`, `extension/translation-scheduler.js`, `extension/graph.js`, `extension/graph-runtime.js`.
